facts.fact: The World Bank diagnostic says the country lacks a unified, digitalised civil registry: there are seven regional offices, each collecting and storing data by manual, paper-based processes, and local judges registering at commune level share manually collected data with those seven offices (no date given; dated to the document's published year).
facts.system: Civil registry (seven regional offices and commune-level judges)

facts.fact: The World Bank diagnostic says the Ministry of Justice, with UNICEF, launched the digital civil registry pilot SIREC in late 2018 exclusively in the capital Malabo, and that funding to expand the digital registry to the mainland is lacking; no office count is given.

The World Bank diagnostic says the SIREC pilot in Malabo allows the digital registration of new births, describes the platform as the one developed to collect new births and deaths, and reports UNICEF as saying it is operational and functions well (no date given; dated to the document's published year).
The World Bank diagnostic says the Ministry of Justice is responsible for civil registration and vital statistics and launched SIREC in late 2018, in collaboration with UNICEF.

The World Bank diagnostic says funding to expand the digital registry to the mainland is currently lacking and names no budget line or funder for SIREC beyond UNICEF's collaboration and support (no date given; dated to the document's published year).

systems.country_label: SIREC; Sistema Informático del Registro Civil
systems.owner: Ministry of Justice, in collaboration with UNICEF
systems.tiers: a pilot exclusively in the capital Malabo since late 2018; not expanded to the mainland; the seven regional offices work on paper

systems.system: Digitisation of historic civil registry records (under the SIREC pilot)
systems.owner: Ministry of Justice with UNICEF; CNIAPGE working on integrating the archives with the SIREC platform
systems.tiers: Malabo; a trained team standardising and digitising historic manual records, not yet accessible on the platform that collects new births and deaths

systems.system: Collection of new-birth data at the principal hospital in Malabo, with standardised manuals
systems.tiers: the principal hospital in Malabo; whether the birth is registered there or notified is not stated

systems.system: CNEDOGE internal database of document issuance
systems.owner: Centro Nacional de Emisión de Documentos Oficiales de Guinea Ecuatorial (CNEDOGE)
systems.tiers: internal to CNEDOGE, active since 2018; national identity card coverage among adults put at about 63 per cent

note: The diagnostic also states that the civil registry has no interoperability with the national identity management system or any sectoral ministry, and that the 2023 household survey found 65.7 per cent of the population with a birth certificate, higher on Bioko than in the continental provinces; neither is a fact under an aspect of this study.
